bands.name: 160 m
bands.purpose: Long-range night-time contacts and regional nets.
bands.notes: MF band. Strong atmospheric noise in summer; large antennas needed.

bands.name: 80 m
bands.purpose: Regional contacts at night, emergency and club nets.
bands.notes: Daytime absorption is high; useful in the evening and at night.

bands.name: 40 m
bands.purpose: All-round DX and regional band, open day and night.
bands.notes: Shares spectrum with broadcast stations in parts of the world.

bands.name: 30 m
bands.purpose: Reliable DX band with low power-friendly conditions.
bands.notes: Narrow band; telephony is not used here.

bands.name: 20 m
bands.notes: Often open worldwide in daylight when solar activity is moderate.

bands.name: 17 m
bands.purpose: Quieter DX band between 20 m and 15 m.

bands.name: 15 m
bands.purpose: Daytime DX when solar activity is good.
bands.notes: Can be dead at solar minimum.

bands.name: 12 m
bands.purpose: Daytime DX during good solar conditions.
bands.notes: Often empty; opens briefly with strong propagation.

bands.name: 10 m
bands.purpose: DX at solar maximum; local FM and repeaters in some regions.
bands.notes: Sporadic-E openings are possible in summer.

bands.name: 6 m
bands.purpose: The 'magic band': sporadic-E and occasional long-distance openings.
bands.notes: Allocation differs a lot between countries; the range shown is only a reference.

bands.name: 2 m
bands.typicalModes: FM, SSB, CW, DMR, C4FM, D-STAR, APRS
bands.purpose: Local communication, repeaters, satellites, weak-signal work.
bands.notes: IARU Region 1 reference range. APRS and repeater sub-bands are defined by the band plan.

bands.name: 70 cm
bands.typicalModes: FM, DMR, D-STAR, C4FM, SSB, ATV
bands.purpose: Local communication, digital voice repeaters and hotspots, satellites.
bands.notes: IARU Region 1 reference range. Repeater offsets and digital sub-bands depend on the national plan.

digitalModes.name: DMR
digitalModes.summary: Digital Mobile Radio: a two-slot TDMA digital voice standard used on many amateur repeaters.
digitalModes.principle: Two voice or data channels share one 12.5 kHz carrier by time slots. Each repeater has a color code; networks route traffic by talkgroup ID.
digitalModes.uses: Local and worldwide voice via repeaters and hotspots, SMS-style text, GPS position reports.
digitalModes.equipment: A DMR handheld or mobile (codeplug with correct frequencies, color code, slot and talkgroups) or a hotspot connected to the internet.

digitalModes.name: D-STAR
digitalModes.summary: Digital Smart Technologies for Amateur Radio: digital voice and data developed in Japan.
digitalModes.principle: Uses GMSK modulation with AMBE voice coding. Callsign routing is built into the protocol header.
digitalModes.equipment: A D-STAR capable radio, or a hotspot with an adapter.

digitalModes.name: C4FM / System Fusion
digitalModes.summary: Yaesu System Fusion: digital voice using 4-level FSK (C4FM) in a 12.5 kHz channel.
digitalModes.principle: Voice and data are sent together; radios fall back to analog FM automatically on analog repeaters.
digitalModes.uses: Local repeater voice, WIRES-X internet linking, group rooms.
digitalModes.equipment: A System Fusion radio (digital and analog capable) or a hotspot.

digitalModes.name: APRS
digitalModes.summary: Automatic Packet Reporting System: position, weather and short messages over AX.25 packet radio.
digitalModes.principle: 1200 baud AFSK packets on a shared frequency, relayed by digipeaters and gated to the internet by iGates.
digitalModes.uses: Tracking vehicles and balloons, weather stations, short messages, emergency communication.
digitalModes.equipment: A radio with a tracker or TNC, a smartphone with a sound-card modem, or an APRS-capable handheld. A receiver is enough for monitoring.

digitalModes.name: FT8
digitalModes.summary: Weak-signal digital mode from the WSJT-X suite with 15-second transmit slots.
digitalModes.principle: Short, forward-error-corrected messages use 8-FSK; decoding works well below the noise floor. Accurate time sync is required.
digitalModes.uses: HF and 6 m DX with low power, band-condition checks.
digitalModes.equipment: An SSB transceiver, a computer with a sound interface, WSJT-X and accurate time (NTP or GPS).

digitalModes.name: JS8Call
digitalModes.summary: Keyboard-to-keyboard messaging built on the FT8 modulation, with store-and-forward relay.
digitalModes.principle: Uses FT8-like transmissions with slower speed options and a messaging layer on top.
digitalModes.uses: Low-power HF messaging and relays when the internet is unavailable.
digitalModes.equipment: An SSB transceiver, a computer with a sound interface and the JS8Call software.

digitalModes.name: M17
digitalModes.summary: Open-source digital voice and data protocol with no proprietary vocoder.
digitalModes.principle: 4FSK modulation, open Codec2 voice coding and an open specification.
digitalModes.uses: Experimental repeaters, hotspots and homebrew radios.
digitalModes.equipment: An M17-capable radio or hotspot firmware.

digitalModes.name: Winlink
digitalModes.summary: Global radio email system used for emergency and off-grid communication.
digitalModes.principle: Messages are exchanged with gateway stations using packet, VARA, ARDOP or Pactor links.
digitalModes.uses: Email over radio, emergency communications, maritime and remote operation.
digitalModes.equipment: A transceiver, a computer or smartphone with a modem and the Winlink Express or compatible client.
